answer: Because the glacier calculation reruns each epoch, the wander weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the basalt settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 170 clones thus holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 35% independent neighbours on the funding graph. That is 34 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
